description: Thai tax residency threshold and related mid-year/VAT filing thresholds that depend on residency-adjacent status.

rules.rule: Thai tax residency threshold (days in Thailand)
rules.conditions: Aggregate days (not necessarily consecutive) physically present in Thailand within a calendar tax year make the individual a Thai tax resident for that year.

source.label: Thai Revenue Department (EN) — Revenue Code Section 41

rules.verification_notes: Directly confirmed on RD's own English page, which states verbatim: 'Any person staying in Thailand for a period or periods aggregating 180 days or more in any tax year shall be deemed a resident of Thailand.' A genuine primary-source citation.

rules.rule: PND94 mid-year filing threshold — single / no qualifying spouse condition
rules.conditions: Jan–Jun income from Section 40(5)-40(8) qualifying types exceeding this amount triggers mid-year PND94 filing.

source.label: MBMG Group; Expat Tax Thailand (secondary, citing Revenue Code Sec. 56/56 bis)

rules.verification_notes: Consistent across two independent secondary sources. RD's own PND94 instruction PDF exists (rd.go.th/fileadmin/download/english_form/080966Ins94.pdf) but its text could not be machine-extracted during this research pass to directly quote the threshold.

rules.rule: PND94 mid-year filing threshold — married, spouse has no income
rules.conditions: Applies when married and spouse has no income; Jan–Jun qualifying income exceeding this amount triggers mid-year PND94 filing.

source.label: MBMG Group; Expat Tax Thailand (secondary, citing Revenue Code Sec. 56/56 bis)

rules.value: September 30 of the tax year (paper filing)
rules.conditions: Paper-filing deadline is solid. An e-filing extension to approximately October 8 exists but depends on a periodically-renewed Ministry of Finance notification (currently Notification No. 7, covering e-filings made 1 Feb 2024 – 31 Jan 2027) — NOT a permanent statutory rule.
rules.verification_notes: September 30 paper deadline is well corroborated. The current e-filing extension window comfortably covers the 2026 half-year filing (due ~Sept/Oct 2026). App does not currently model the e-filing extension separately — only the paper due date is stored.

rules.value: March 31 of the following year (paper filing)
rules.conditions: Standard annual PIT filing deadline for paper filing is solid law. An e-filing extension of ~8 days to early April exists historically but depends on a periodically-renewed Ministry of Finance notification, NOT permanent statute.
rules.verification_notes: IMPORTANT UNCERTAINTY FOUND: March 31 is solidly confirmed. However, the current e-filing extension notification (No. 7, dated 12 Jan 2024) only covers e-filings made through 31 January 2027. The tax-year-2026 annual return would be e-filed Feb-Apr 2027 — AFTER that cutoff. Based on the historical pattern (a prior notification, No. 3, similarly expired and was renewed as No. 7), a renewal before Feb 2027 is likely but NOT YET CONFIRMED by any notification found during this research pass. Treat the e-filing extension as 'expected based on historical pattern, unconfirmed for tax year 2026 filings' rather than settled fact. The app's stored PND90_91_DUE_DATE (2027-03-31) reflects only the solid paper deadline, which is correct either way.

rules.rule: Income types that trigger PND94 mid-year filing obligation
rules.conditions: Only these four Section 40 categories count toward the PND94 Jan-Jun threshold check — salary (40(1)) and dividend income do not.
rules.verification_notes: The app's current list matches both independent secondary sources exactly.
